resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO), Resale / Rental Certificate
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Maywood Construction Official (Building Department / Department of Code Enforcement)
resale_co.lead_time: Under the Borough Code, the owner allows the inspection within 5 days of paying the fee and applying, and the certificate (or a 14-day temporary certificate, or a denial) is issued within 5 days of the inspection.
resale_co.valid_for: Expires if the home is not occupied within six months of issuance
requirements: Separate smoke/CO certificate of compliance from the Fire Prevention Bureau (the Borough calls it the "Smoke Certificate for CCO")
Handrails secured on any stair with 3 or more risers or over 24 inches high, including attic, basement and exterior stairs; no temporary wood railings
Front door deadbolt may not be keyed on both sides
No open slots in the main electric panel; GFI outlets required
Traps on all sinks, toilets, baths and showers; gas valves on all appliances and unused gas lines capped
Chimney base sealed around smoke pipes; boiler and water heater smoke pipes screwed at all joints
Permits and final inspections closed for any construction work, water heater or boiler replacement
Sump pumps must discharge outside, not into the house sewer
Shrubs within 10 feet of a roadway (25 feet of an intersection) no taller than 3 1/2 feet
House number at least 3 inches high, visible from the street
Sidewalks may not be lifted, broken or cracked; soil movement will be inspected; Borough property maintenance code applies inside and out

fees.label: Certificate of continued occupancy, one-family structure
Certificate of continued occupancy, multiple dwellings

resale_co.how_to_apply: Get the original Resale / Rental Certificate application at Borough Hall, 15 Park Avenue (only a sample is posted online), and file it with the Building Department with the fee. A separate application and fee for the smoke/CO certificate go to the Fire Prevention Bureau (Borough Hall, 3rd floor). Building inspections are requested by email; building inspection hours are Tuesday and Thursday 3 to 6 pm.
resale_co.contact_title: Construction Official & Building Inspector (Zoning Official/Inspector: Dina Lynch, dlynch@maywoodboro.org)

evidence.quote: No owner shall sell, rent or lease any dwelling unit to any person intending to use the dwelling unit for residential purposes, or allow any person to inhabit any dwelling unit, or sell, rent, lease or allow the occupancy of a nonresidential unit, unless the owner has obtained from the Construction Official a certificate of continued occupancy.

If a dwelling unit or nonresidential unit is not occupied within six months of the issuance of a certificate of continued occupancy, the certificate will expire, and a new certificate must be obtained before occupancy.

Within five days of the receipt of the payment of the required fee and the required application form, the owner shall afford the Construction Official the opportunity to inspect the structure and shall consent to the inspection.
Sample Resale and Rental Certificate Application
The original must be obtained at Borough Hall
The following list is only a guideline and should not be considered all-inclusive. If any of the items listed below are not completed a CCO will not be issued.
Construction Official & Building Inspector Gary Goodman

resale_co.notes: Borough Code Chapter 141 (Certificate of Continued Occupancy, Ord. No. 18-93) and fee Section 169 (amended through Ord. No. 11-25, July 22, 2025) were read through the ecode360 print view. The fee table lists one-family $50 and multiple dwellings $50 per unit; it has no separate two-family line, although the application form has a Two Family box, so confirm the two-family fee. The Building Department page now lists Gary Goodman as Construction Official; the sample checklist PDF still names Phil Cheff, (201) 845-2900 ext. 4. Page 1 of the sample application is a scanned image. Rental CCOs fall under the same chapter; rental-only items are not listed here.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level including the basement and habitable attic, outside each sleeping area within 10 feet, and in any room with a fuel-fired fireplace
Smoke alarms must be less than 10 years old and UL listed; battery alarms must be sealed 10-year units; 110-volt interconnected systems may not be converted to battery alarms
Carbon monoxide alarms on all levels with sleeping areas, within 10 feet of all sleeping areas; CO alarms must be less than seven (7) years old
Portable fire extinguisher, at least 2A-10:BC, no more than 10 pounds, mounted in or within 10 feet of the kitchen near an exit path (form still lists it)

fire_cert.notes: The posted smoke application ("Sample Smoke Certificate for CCO", scanned image PDF from 2022, guideline page revised 1/2020) lists $50.00 / $85.00 / $140.00 by business days between application and inspection. Borough Code Section 179-10 says the CSDCMAC fee is charged at the state rate in N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9, so current fees may follow the state schedule; confirm. The form still lists a portable fire extinguisher, which state law (P.L.2025, c.19) dropped from the sale certificate in February 2025. The state directory lists the Building Department (15 Park Av) as the smoke detector compliance office; fireinspector@maywoodboro.org is the fire inspector email on the Building Department page. The scanned fee table uses dot leaders between each row label and its amount, so the fee quotes give the row label only.
